polarization_separate — SPECULAR polarization op

• 数据种类:polsweep → image2d

• 调用: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.polarization_separate(images, angles_deg=(0.0, 45.0, 90.0, 135.0), max_violation_frac=0.0)(要直接调用实现,import specularity; specularity.polarization_separate(images, angles_deg=(0.0, 45.0, 90.0, 135.0), max_violation_frac=0.0);从台账取用则 opsspecular.get("polarization_separate"))

• 经台账调用的返回值: fullseye.ledger.polarization_separate(...) 只返回声明的 out 类型 image2d 的值(底层函数还会返回辅助信息)。需要被丢弃的部分时,使用 fullseye.ledger.polarization_separate.raw(...),或直接调用 specularity.polarization_separate。

用法

把偏振片旋转序列分成非偏振与线偏振的辐亮度。→ (diffuse, specular),都是 (H, W)。

> 以下的详细说明为原文 —— 摘要与标题已翻译。

Fitting I(t) = 0.5 (S0 + S1 cos 2t + S2 sin 2t) per pixel gives I_min and I_max in closed form, and the classical separation (Wolff & Boult 1991; Nayar, Fang & Boult 1997) reads

diffuse = 2 * I_min (the unpolarised radiance)

specular = I_max - I_min (the linearly polarised radiance)

with diffuse + specular = I_min + I_max = the total scene radiance, so nothing is lost or invented. Round-tripping polarization_render through this operator returns the inputs with a maximum absolute error of 3.9e-16 for the four angles of a division-of-focal-plane sensor and 4.4e-16 for a bare three-angle sweep (measured in tests/test_specularity.py).

Read the names as shorthand. What is recovered exactly is the unpolarised and polarised parts. Calling them diffuse and specular assumes diffuse reflection is unpolarised and specular reflection is fully linearly polarised — true near Brewster's angle for a dielectric, false at normal incidence, where the specular reflection is unpolarised and this operator returns all of it as "diffuse", and unreliable for metals. The polarisation route is complementary to the colour route (specular_diffuse_split), not a replacement: it needs no illuminant colour and works on textured, multi-material surfaces, but it needs a favourable geometry.

*max_violation_frac* is the fraction of pixels allowed to fit a negative minimum radiance before the call fails. The default 0 is fail-closed: a negative fitted minimum means the modulation exceeded the mean, which no analyser can produce, and it usually means the frames and *angles_deg* are out of order. Raise it to clamp sensor-noise-level violations to zero as a deliberate, recorded choice.

What value to raise it to (measured 2026-09-15). Violations come from pixels whose *unpolarised* radiance sits at the noise floor, not from the noise level as such: uniform scenes with unpolarised fraction ≥ 0.2 show 0.0000 violations at 0.5–5 % noise, and only a scene that is almost fully polarised (unpolarised fraction 0.05) fails (2 % noise → 0.0018, 5 % → 0.13). On a gradient scene (unpolarised radiance 0 → 0.6, absolute noise σ, four angles) the violation fraction tracks the share of pixels with D < 2σ: σ=0.005 → 0.0076 (2σ share 0.023), σ=0.01 → 0.015 (0.039), σ=0.02 → 0.025 (0.070), σ=0.05 → 0.058 (0.172). So estimate the share of pixels darker than 2–3 σ and set *max_violation_frac* to that; the full table is in docs/ops/specular/guides/specular_photometric.md. The frame-order claim above is weaker than it reads: with equally spaced angles (0/45/90/135, 0/60/120, and also 0/30/90/135 and 0/20/45/90/160) every permutation of a noise-free sweep still fits a non-negative minimum (all permutations measured, violation 0.0000) — a wrong order looks like a correct sweep at another azimuth, so the order is metadata this check cannot recover.

Negative frames (2026-10-24). A pixel with a frame value below -POLAR_NEGATIVE_FLOOR * max|I| (2 % of the stack's largest magnitude) is a violation too, in the same *max_violation_frac* budget: a negative radiance is not a scene, and polarization_render refuses it in the forward direction. The floor leaves room for the read noise of dark-frame-subtracted data; the reasoning is at POLAR_NEGATIVE_FLOOR.

Raises ValueError: *images* is not an (N, H, W) stack of at least 3 frames, has no pixels, or exceeds MAX_LIGHTS / MAX_STACK_ELEMENTS; *angles_deg* does not match the frame count, leaves the fit rank-deficient (two angles equal modulo 180) or ill-conditioned (condition number over POLAR_DESIGN_MAX_COND), or has every angle at most 2*pi in magnitude (radians passed as degrees); more than *max_violation_frac* of the pixels fit a negative minimum or have a frame below the negative floor.
